History:
- Main complaints: Low mood, decreased appetite, low energy, headaches, and nausea.
- Onset/progression: Symptoms of low mood and low energy began approximately 3.5 months ago, coinciding with change to new law firm; weight loss began around 6 months ago.
- Weight loss: Approximately 1 stone (~14 lbs) over 6 months.
- Associated symptoms: Reduced appetite, occasional nausea (not linked to specific foods), palpitations and sensation of shortness of breath (not on walking, more pronounced in elevators/lifts or stressful environments), occasional feeling unwell, no vomiting, no chest pain, no acid reflux.
- Bowel habits: Normal; no diarrhea, no blood or mucus, no pain on defecation.
- Functional impact: Some difficulties with energy at work and at home; decreased engagement in daily activities.
- No specific triggers identified. No previous similar episodes reported.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid); previously on thyroxine.
- Stopped taking thyroxine since changing doctors (timeline not specified).
- Last thyroid blood test: Not performed in a long time.
- Medications: Previously thyroxine; not currently taking any medications (except possibly thyroxine, currently stopped; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Not mentioned.
- Previous hospitalizations: Not mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- No acute physical findings reported or observed in transcript.
- Denies chest pain, denies diarrhea, denies vomiting, denies blood/mucus in stool.
- No throat swelling, no mention of skin changes.
- Alert and oriented during consult.
- No issues with mobility, able to walk a mile without shortness of breath when feeling well (although not recently attempted due to poor health).
- Palpitations and sensation of breathlessness primarily occur in elevators/lifts; no syncope reported.
- No acute distress noted during virtual assessment.

Impression:
- Low mood and reduced energy with weight loss and nausea; hypothyroidism off treatment; nonspecific complaints. Differential includes depressive disorder, hypothyroidism relapse, nutritional deficiencies, or other systemic causes.

Management Plan:
- Arrange general blood tests (including thyroid function, anemia screen, kidney and liver function, vitamin levels).
- Advised patient to call support number (via app) to arrange blood test.
- Instructed to promptly seek medical attention if chest pain, palpitations, vomiting, or changes in bowel habits develop.
- Plan to review once blood test results available; will receive a text message to schedule follow-up.

Patient Summary:
- Patient reports several months of low mood, fatigue, reduced appetite, weight loss, and occasional palpitations and nausea; has stopped his thyroid medication. Blood tests have been arranged to investigate possible causes, including thyroid dysfunction and other systemic illnesses. Follow-up will depend on investigation results.

Key Takeaways:
- Arrange and complete recommended blood tests promptly.
- Seek urgent care if developing chest pain, persisting palpitations, vomiting, or changes in bowel habits.
- Await communication for follow-up after results; do not delay in reaching out if condition worsens.

Next Steps:
- Complete blood work as directed.
- Book follow-up appointment after receiving results (via text/app notification).
- Reinitiate thyroid medication only after re-evaluation and confirmation from care provider.

Quality checks (document_quality):

- Missing elements: Allergies not addressed; full medication reconciliation not performed; social history, alcohol/smoking status, and family history not explored.
- Internal conflicts: None detected.
- Transcript quality: Good; minor sections with unclear or truncated patient speech, but clinically relevant information well conveyed.
